subject: Reseller patent assertion: routing & proposed indemnity split

Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Mendax IP assertion re: reseller distribution

Jonas — I reviewed Mendax's letter and the current Order Form language. High-level thoughts:

- Mendax's assertion is broad but currently factual evidence is limited (claims reference feature X in a regional deployment).
- Our standard indemnity obligates us to defend and indemnify customers/resellers for third-party IP claims "arising from use of the Service as permitted in the Agreement." The reseller flow has a reseller addendum; it is not explicit about defense-control for channel partners.

Risk/option matrix:
1) Accept defense/control and manage litigation — exposure to defense costs and potential settlement (we control strategy).
2) Offer cost-sharing (50/50) for defense costs with the reseller while retaining final defense-control for material decisions. This reduces Redwood's near-term spend and preserves strategic control.
3) Offer indemnity only if reseller can prove they used the product strictly in accordance with our published integration guide (i.e., no custom patches).

Given Acme's request for an immediate confirmation, I recommend we propose option 2 as a temporary bridge: Redwood takes lead on defense, but costs are split 50/50 during initial discovery; if evidence shows reseller misuse, Redwood reserves right to seek reimbursement. Also propose a short term hold on distribution with a 7-day remediation window.

I'll draft proposed language for an Order Form addendum and a redline to circulate. Need sales to confirm whether Acme will accept cost-splitting and to capture any contractual constraints from their procurement terms.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-18T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Mendax IP assertion re: reseller distribution

Adding a proposed redline for the Order Form that inserts a reseller-specific indemnity paragraph and a provisional defense-cost allocation. Key points in the draft:

- Redwood agrees to defend Third-Party IP claims "relating to the Service" but defense-control for distributor/reseller claims is retained by Redwood; Redwood may delegate litigation to outside counsel it selects.
- During the initial 90 days of a claim, Redwood and the reseller split reasonable defense costs 50/50 unless reseller's misuse/contribution is shown.
- If reseller's configuration or redistribution outside the scope of the Order Form contributed to the claim, Redwood may seek reimbursement.
- Timeline: we are proposing a 7-business-day acknowledgement window and 30-day initial fact-gathering period before any distribution pause beyond temporary suspension.

Attached: redline_orderform_reseller.docx

If Acme won't accept the provisional split, we should escalate to BizOps/legal leadership; otherwise this language should be acceptable as a short-term compromise while we investigate.

Kimberly Park
VP, Legal
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Ramos <procurement@acmereseller.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed short-term indemnity arrangement (Mendax IP claim)

Eve — thanks for flagging and forwarding the Mendax letter. We want to resolve this quickly to avoid disruption to your distribution.

Redwood's legal team proposes the following interim approach while we investigate the underlying facts:

- Redwood will assume control of the defense for the Mendax assertion.
- Defense costs will be provisionally split 50/50 between Redwood and Acme for the initial fact-gathering phase (30 days), unless investigation shows Acme materially deviated from the approved integration.
- Redwood reserves the right to seek reimbursement if reseller misuse is established.
- We propose a 7-business-day window for acknowledgement and a short pause on any new distribution if necessary; current active distribution can continue under a good-faith cooperation plan while we collect evidence.

Attached is a draft snippet for insertion into the Order Form if Acme agrees. Please let us know by EOD tomorrow whether Acme can accept this provisional split and the proposed timeline. If not, we'll escalate to our VP Legal to discuss alternate options.

Attachments: redline_orderform_reseller.docx

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Strategic Partners
Redwood Inference

From: Eve Ramos <procurement@acmereseller.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-19T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed short-term indemnity arrangement (Mendax IP claim)

Jonas — thanks for the quick response and for looping in legal. We reviewed the provisional 50/50 split and have two immediate concerns:

1) Acme cannot commit to sharing defense costs on a 50/50 basis without explicit carveouts for reseller-conduct vs product defects. Our procurement legal says Redwood should absorb defense costs unless the reseller materially altered the product or engaged in unauthorized distribution.
2) The proposed possibility of suspending distribution is a non-starter unless Redwood provides indemnity for lost margin during the suspension period.

We attached a short timeline the procurement team needs for our execs. We're open to a short-term cooperation plan (sharing documents, quick evidence collection), but we need Redwood to: (a) lead defense with control over settlement thresholds (we cannot be put on the hook for settlement decisions), and (b) accept commercial risk for suspension-related lost margin if Redwood requests a pause.

Attached: acme_timeline.xlsx

If Redwood can confirm defense-control and absorb suspension losses (subject to review), Acme will cooperate with an expedited investigation. Otherwise our next step is to pause distribution within 48 hours pending contractual clarity.

Eve Ramos
Head of Procurement
Acme Reseller Inc.
